# Task 86c: upload money fixes (repo LectorIA-meta, branch fix/upload-money)

Architecture review of the merged upload backend (server/uploads/*, core/uploads.ts,
docs/uploads.md) found four money/abuse bugs. Fix all four with tests (Meta, Jev,
Blob, Redis, Turnstile mocked; reuse server/uploads/test-support.ts fakes). Keep
the public API and error codes unchanged.

1. Reserve sizing and leaks. `UPLOAD_RESERVE_MICRO = 250_000` is a flat USD 0.25
   hold (~10x real cost: a 3,955-word book measured USD 0.0027) and is only released
   at the winning finalize or in failJob. Abandoned jobs and the repair branch in
   server/uploads/step.ts (~lines 148-154) keep it, in both the daily uploads key and
   the shared overall spend cap. Fix: size the hold in createUpload from parts count
   and/or word count (a few thousand micro per part, a floor of ~50_000 micro, a
   ceiling that keeps a 50k-word free book well under the USD 1/day cap; document
   the formula with the measured cost). Reconcile `usageCostMicro(usage) - reservedMicro`
   in the repair branch too. Also have the daily cleanup cron
   (server/uploads/cleanup.ts) reconcile jobs still `working` older than ~6 hours:
   adjust the reservation to their recorded usage and mark them expired/failed
   (exactly once, idempotent).
2. failJob (step.ts ~105-129) refunds all of reservedMicro and the book quota while
   ignoring job.usage, so a user can loop spend past the caps by forcing failures.
   Fix: adjust spend by `usageCostMicro(usage) - reservedMicro` (keep what was really
   spent), and refund the book quota only when recorded usage is zero.
3. Concurrency. stepUpload does a last-writer-wins kv.set of job usage under a
   per-part lock, so parallel steps lose usage. Fix: store per-part usage in each
   part result blob (or a per-part KV key) and sum it in finalize, so finalize (and
   the fail/cleanup reconcile paths, which must sum the same way) is the only money
   writer. `uploadFinalizeKey` is setNxEx with a 30-day TTL: make it a ~90 s lease
   so a finalize killed at the 60 s function limit doesn't leave the job stuck; a
   separate durable "finalized" marker must still guarantee exactly-once spend
   adjustment. Add a test with two parallel steps on different parts proving no
   usage is lost, and one proving a stale finalize lease is retaken.
4. BYOK bypass. Any 8 printable chars in x-byok-key skip all per-person limits.
   Fix: apply a per-person create quota to BYOK too (10/day per hashed IP or anon
   cookie via bookQuotaKeysFor/takeDualQuota with a distinct key prefix, e.g.
   `upload:byok:`), spend still free for us; refund that quota on create failure.
   Map exhaustion to the existing daily_books_reached code.

1|# Upload processing API
2|
3|Server path turning a browser-parsed EPUB into reader data. The browser
4|parses the file with `core/epub.ts` and POSTs the sections; the server
5|cleans, segments, and classifies one chapter-part per call so every
6|request finishes inside the Hobby 60 s budget.
7|
8|## Create
9|
10|`POST /api/uploads`, JSON body:
11|
12|```json
13|{ "title": "Middlemarch", "author": "George Eliot", "sections": [RawSection], "turnstileToken": "…" }
14|```
15|
16|`sections` is the `RawSection[]` shape from `core/clean-types.ts`. Limits:
17|50k words free, 400k with a key; 600 sections; 20k chars per block; 4 MB
18|body. BYOK sends its key per call in the `x-byok-key` header (in memory
19|only, never stored). Needs same-origin JSON plus the Turnstile/human
20|cookie flow shared with chat and images.
21|
22|Success: `{ "status": "created", "id": "u-…", "chapters": 24, "parts": 24 }`.
23|The id is a 128-bit capability; free jobs also bind the anon cookie.
24|The cleaning judge gets 25 s inside this request; past that the book
25|keeps its deterministic chapters.
26|
27|## Step
28|
29|`POST /api/uploads/<id>/step`, body `{}` or `{ "chapter": 3 }` with an
30|optional `turnstileToken` when the human cookie expired. Processes the next
31|pending part (segment + emotion) and stores it. BYOK repeats the key header;
32|free repeats the cookies.
33|
34|- `{ "status": "working", "id": "u-…", "done": 3, "total": 24 }` — call again.
35|- `{ "status": "done", "id": "u-…", "done": 24, "total": 24, "costUsd": 0.021 }`
36|  — the analysis is assembled; `costUsd` is the real Meta+Jev cost.
37|
38|Re-driving a finished part or job is idempotent and free. Music needs no
39|step: scenes carry the same `final` emotion vectors Oz has, so the
40|existing track selection scores them unchanged.
41|
42|## Errors
43|
44|`{ "status": "error", "code": "<code>", "message": "…" }`. Codes: `too_long`
45|(use BYOK, 413), `daily_books_reached` (2/day, 429), `daily_budget_reached`
46|(503), `human_required` (403), `bad_request` (400), `unavailable` (503,
47|refunded), `not_found` (404), `expired` (30 days, 410).
48|
49|## Reading and cleanup
50|
51|`loadUploadedBook(id)` in `server/uploads/loader.ts` returns the
52|`BookPayload` the reader consumes (`{ book, scenes }`). Uploads expire
53|after 30 days; `GET /api/cron/cleanup-uploads` (Bearer `CRON_SECRET`,
54|daily) deletes their private blobs.
55|
56|## Storage
57|
58|Uploads live in a separate private Blob store, not the public image
59|store: a store's access mode is fixed at creation, so `access: "private"`
60|puts would fail against it. The token comes from
61|`UPLOADS_BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` (passed explicitly to every Blob call)
62|and the owner creates the store by hand. Without the token the routes
63|answer `unavailable`; they never fall back to the public store.

1|# Design: task 86 upload processing
2|
3|Goal: server path turning a browser-parsed EPUB into the same data a shelf
4|book has (`BookPayload`: book + analyzed scenes), behind free/BYOK caps, one
5|chapter-part per request so every call finishes under the 60 s Hobby budget.
6|
7|## API
8|
9|- `POST /api/uploads` — body `{title, author?, sections, turnstileToken?}`
10|  where `sections` is the browser's parsed EPUB sections (`RawSection[]`).
11|  Validates, cleans (deterministic + contributor judge), takes quota/spend
12|  (free only), stores `book.json` in private Blob, job state in Redis.
13|  Returns `{status:"created", id, chapters, parts}`.
14|- `POST /api/uploads/<id>/step` — body `{}` or `{chapter}`. Segments and
15|  classifies the next pending part (or that chapter's next part), stores the
16|  part result. Returns `{status:"working", id, done, total}` or
17|  `{status:"done", id, done, total, costUsd}` after finalizing.
18|- `GET /api/cron/cleanup-uploads` — deletes `uploads/` blobs older than 30
19|  days. Bearer `CRON_SECRET`, daily schedule in `vercel.json`.
20|
21|Full contract in `docs/uploads.md`. Reader entry: `loadUploadedBook(id)`
22|in `server/uploads/loader.ts` (wired into `server/books.ts` later, by owner).
23|
24|## Flow
25|
26|Create: same-origin + body cap + strict parse → env → Turnstile →
27|anon cookie → BYOK header? → deterministic clean + word count
28|(`too_long` past 50k free / 400k BYOK) → quota (2/day, IP or cookie) →
29|spend reserve ($0.25 flat, total + `upload:spend:daily` caps) → judge →
30|build book + textVersion → split parts (≤150 paras) → Blob + Redis.
31|
32|Step: guards as above → load job (free jobs bind the anon cookie, BYOK
33|jobs need the key header per call) → next pending part → Redis lock →
34|re-check part blob (idempotent, free) → segment via exported
35|`chapterPrompt`/`parseScenes` + `validateSceneCoverage` (one retry) →
36|classify each scene (Jev + `classifyScene` override when a server Jev key
37|exists, else contributor-only vector; per-scene errors keep `final: null`
38|like Oz) → store part → finalize under a guard when all parts land
39|(assign `c<ch>s<k>` ids, `validateBookCoverage`, `adjust` real spend).
40|
41|Music: Oz has no stored cluster at runtime; the reader scores each scene's
42|`final` vector against the manifest (`rankScored`). Uploads reuse that path
43|by producing the same `final` shape. No new music code.
44|

2|
3|Server path turning a browser-parsed EPUB into reader data. The browser
4|parses the file with `core/epub.ts` and POSTs the sections; the server

7|
8|## Create
9|
10|`POST /api/uploads`, JSON body:
11|
12|```json
13|{ "title": "Middlemarch", "author": "George Eliot", "sections": [RawSection], "turnstileToken": "…" }
14|```
15|
16|`sections` is the `RawSection[]` shape from `core/clean-types.ts`. Limits:
17|50k words free, 400k with a key; 600 sections; 20k chars per block; 4 MB
18|body. BYOK sends its key per call in the `x-byok-key` header (in memory
19|only, never stored). Needs same-origin JSON plus the Turnstile/human
20|cookie flow shared with chat and images.
21|
22|Success: `{ "status": "created", "id": "u-…", "chapters": 24, "parts": 24 }`.
23|The id is a 128-bit capability; free jobs also bind the anon cookie.
24|The cleaning judge gets 25 s inside this request; past that the book
25|keeps its deterministic chapters.
26|
27|## Step
28|
29|`POST /api/uploads/<id>/step`, body `{}` or `{ "chapter": 3 }` with an
30|optional `turnstileToken` when the human cookie expired. Processes the next
31|pending part (segment + emotion) and stores it. BYOK repeats the key header;
32|free repeats the cookies.
33|

35|- `{ "status": "done", "id": "u-…", "done": 24, "total": 24, "costUsd": 0.021 }`

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.

  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.
- Trace the real flow: where data comes in, what is stored, what goes out.
- A change can break code it does not touch. When a signature, return value
  or behavior changes, grep every caller.

1. **Bug:** wrong result, crash, missed edge case (empty, zero, last item,
   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
